items.title: Webinar: The Insider's Guide to Leveraging Podcasts, Webinars and Thought Leadership Programs
items.snippet: Join BioSpace's Managing Editor, Director of Insights and Vice President of Marketing for an inside look at how PR, communications and marketing teams can successfully leverage webinars, podcasts and integrated content campaigns to elevate executive voices, share industry expertise and engage key biotech and pharma au...

items.title: Samsung Biologics inks $262M manufacturing deal with European pharma company
items.snippet: The agreement, which runs through 2033, comes as Samsung Biologics continues to expand its large manufacturing footprint in South Korea.

items.title: Disc sets up polycythemia vera challenge but Silence maintains lead
items.snippet: The polycythemia vera field is heating up, with Disc Medicine and Silence Therapeutics each advancing next-generation therapies, playing catch-up to Takeda and Protagonist Therapeutics, who won the FDA’s approval last month for Mimrylo.

items.title: Frazier adds $1.1B+ to small and mid-sized biotech fund
items.snippet: Frazier’s life science fund has already benefited several successful biotechs, including Verona Pharma, which was acquired by Merck for $10 billion, and Carmot Therapeutics, which Roche bought for $2.7 billion.

items.title: Novartis drags peers down with triple asset stumble
items.snippet: Novartis’ shares fell 13% this week after the report of three separate late-stage asset setbacks. The impact went beyond the Swiss drugmaker, dragging peers down across the market.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikahil and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Novartis’ board faces investor scrutiny after M&A misfires and R&D flops
items.snippet: Back-to-back failures of multiple late-phase trials have raised questions about how Novartis has deployed capital in pursuit of drugs to drive growth through the 2030s.

items.title: Takeda’s long-term R&D head announces exit after major pipeline reorganization
items.snippet: A few months after a new CEO stepped up to helm Takeda, the drugmaker will now have to prepare for another leadership change as its long-time R&D head plans his exit.

items.title: Biohaven takes another hit as FDA pauses enrollment in pivotal trials for embattled epilepsy drug
items.snippet: The enrollment pause comes after BHV-7000 failed to show efficacy in a midstage depression trial late last year. The news is another regulatory hit for Biohaven after the FDA declined to approve its spinocerebellar ataxia treatment in November 2025.

items.title: Drugmakers cherry pick launch regions as MFN creates 'policy environment like an earthquake'
items.snippet: With multiple drug pricing initiatives like Most Favored Nation now in force, drugmakers have to reinvent their commercial strategies to stay ahead of the fast-moving policy environment, according to a new report from Numerof & Associates.

items.title: Encoded raises $275M series F for Dravet syndrome gene therapy
items.snippet: Encoded Therapeutics’ lead asset ETX101 is a gene therapy being tested for Dravet syndrome. Phase 1/2 data showed substantial reductions in seizures.

items.title: Tyra shares slip as bladder cancer responses fall short of investor expectations
items.snippet: Despite falling short of analyst expectations, Tyra Biosciences is taking its cancer drug to registrational development for non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.

items.title: The supply chain fault lines of modern pharma
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured, sponsored by SK pharmteco, Jennifer Smith-Parker speaks to Arvind Singh, vice president and global head of supply chain. In this episode, we explore how CDMOs are reshaping supply‑chain strategy for a new generation of complex modalities.

items.title: 11 companies hiring in California now
items.snippet: Looking for a biopharma job in California? Check out the BioSpace list of 11 companies hiring life sciences professionals like you.

items.title: August biopharma layoffs impact just over 500, down 90% year over year
items.snippet: Last month, biotech and pharma companies making or planning workforce cuts included three whose reductions will more than halve their workforces. Blueprint Medicines’ layoffs will affect the most employees.

items.title: From process to intelligence: How AI is reshaping people strategy in life sciences
items.snippet: Applying artificial intelligence and automation tactics has played a large role in talent strategy conversations in the past few years. While many organizations initially focused on experimenting with tools and driving adoption to create efficiencies, leading employers are now asking deeper questions.

items.title: For PDUFA VIII, the most valuable incentive may be time
items.snippet: The FDA’s proposal to offer 50% off application fees for drugs with early-stage trials conducted in the U.S. is unlikely to achieve the intended result. What biotechs really want is speed.

items.title: Merck adds 53 to New Jersey chopping block
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Webinar: The Massive Scale of GLP-1s: Evolving Health, Healthcare and Markets
items.snippet: Watch this discussion on how GLP-1 drugs for obesity are changing the shape of U.S. healthcare. From direct-to-consumer portals to pharmacy deals, how these drugs reach patients is changing—and leading to debates over pricing and coverage. Learn how your company can be both patient-forward while also maximizing revenu...

items.title: Sandoz plans ‘vast and vertically integrated’ supply chain to support 100-biosimilar vision
items.snippet: The company is investing billions of dollars to construct a European biosimilar hub capable of supporting the rapid expansion of its portfolio.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikahil and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

items.title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
items.snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.
